glossary.m: the big lesson a story teaches, said as a full sentence
what a story is about, in a word or two, like loyalty or winter
the words characters say out loud in a story
the marks “ and ” that go around the exact words someone says
the part that tells who is talking, like said Lucy
the main part of a word that holds its meaning, like ject, which means throw
a part added to the front or the end of a word, like un- or -ed
telling the truth, even when it is hard

cards.title: World Notes: Field Mice and the Morning Star
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: Field mice have sharp front teeth that never stop growing. Gnawing keeps them short, and mice can chew right through rope and string.
Just before sunrise, you can sometimes see one very bright star low in the east. Often it is not a star at all. It is the planet Venus, called the morning star.
In Chapter 15, Lucy and Susan see both: little mice, and one big star low in the east as the night ends.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Chapter 15 begins on a sad night and ends at sunrise. Watch what Lucy and Susan see.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: build ject words, fix a line of dialogue, and spell long words from the root.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 15. Then answer three questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you add proof from Chapter 15 to your response.

notes.wordParts: The root ject means throw. reject = throw back. inject = throw into. eject = throw out. project = throw forward.
notes.grammar: Quotation marks go around the exact words someone says. The first word gets a capital. The comma or period goes inside the closing mark: “Let him approach,” said Aslan.
notes.spelling: A long word is often a root with parts added. Find the root first: un + expect + ed = unexpected.
notes.wgrd: The Deeper Magic means a willing, innocent life given for a traitor makes death work backwards. It makes the theme stronger: love is stronger than the Witch's law.
vocab: someone who betrays the trust of their own side
to make up for a wrong you have done
giving up something precious for something or someone more important
coming back to life after death

plate.alt: A painting of a misty harbor at sunrise, with a small orange sun, its reflection on the water, and dark rowboats
plate.credit: Impression, Sunrise · Claude Monet, 1872 · Musée Marmottan Monet, Paris · Public domain
plate.look: A painting by Claude Monet, a French painter, from 1872. The sun is just coming up over the water, small and orange in the mist. People say this painting gave a whole group of painters their name: the Impressionists. In Chapter 15, Lucy and Susan watch the sun come up over the sea.
plate.lookBtn: Tap to learn about this painting of a sunrise

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Susan tells Lucy, “I feel afraid to turn round.”
items.why: She says how she really feels, even though she is scared.

items.t: When Lucy asks if he is dead, Aslan answers her truthfully: “Not now.”
items.why: He gives her a true answer to her question.

items.t: When Susan asks what it all means, Aslan explains the Deeper Magic plainly.
items.why: He tells them the whole truth, so they understand.
